title: the-cairn-device-owns-the-trouble-panel
intention: The cairn device (singleton, instance 0) owns and surfaces the trouble lane on a web pane. Two-sided: list left, detail right, red light at top (bright red if live, dull reddish grey if none). Starts at row 0. Dynamic page.
why: There is no device that means all-of-Cairn. The trouble lane is a runtime thing with no surface — it is read only at session-open hooks and by hand. A panel that shows live troubles with a red light is the normal-operating-state made visible.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth. The trouble panel is a diagnostic surface; it shows the full finding, never a summary.
Law 5 — intent, its state, and its proofs share an address. The cairn device's pane is its surface at its address.
I-the-cairn-device.md child a — the cairn device intention names this pane.

falsifier.proves_green: The panel surfaces live troubles from CairnCommons/troubles/ on a web pane declared by the cairn device. TWO sides: list left (trouble id + short summary), detail right (full finding on click). Red light at top: bright red when any trouble is live, dull reddish grey when none. The panel is a PANE on the one web server — it does not own a route, a port, or a server of its own.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the panel owns its own route/port/server — the one-web-server rule holds, and a device gets a declared PANE, never its own endpoint; (2) the panel does not show live troubles — only showing stale/cached data is not a diagnostic surface; (3) the cairn device is confused with system_rackmount — the host is the laptop, cairn is the project, different scopes, different devices; (4) the trouble detail is truncated or summarized — Law 7 says a diagnostic surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape but the detail view is not a collapse, it is the record; (5) the panel is read-only but does not SAY so — a surface that looks editable but is not is a false affordance.
falsifier.horizon: After the-web-server-graduates-to-starlette — the stdlib web_server is synchronous and cannot do WebSocket push, which the dynamic page needs. This ticket is the Starlette migration's first consumer.

how: Build the cairn device (singleton, instance 0) with a trouble-panel web pane. Two-sided: list left, detail right, red light at top. The device means all-of-Cairn and surfaces the trouble lane.

chart_notes.orient: The trouble store is at CairnCommons/troubles/*.json, already read at session-open by the hook (bin/cmd/session_start_hook). The cairn device is a singleton at instance 0. The pane is a declared shape on the web server, rendered by render.py.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: editing/closing troubles from the panel (read-only surface); owning a route/port/server (pane on the one web server); showing anything other than the trouble store's own records. IN: the two-sided layout, the red light, the WebSocket push for live updates.
chart_notes.validate: A live trouble appears on the panel within one WebSocket push cycle. The red light is bright red with live troubles, dull reddish grey with none. Clicking a trouble in the list shows its full finding in the detail pane. An empty trouble store shows the dull reddish grey light and an empty list.

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: this is a FIXME repair of a ticket whose panel was built and PROVED on 2026-09-04. The pane declaration, the handler, the render kind, the red light, the /ws/troubles route and the probe module ALREADY EXIST and are not rebuilt. The repair is only the probe's carry (D2) and the proof teeth already committed (D3).

D2: SETTLED: apply exactly the unified diff carried in this ticket's build_patch field (`git apply` from a file holding that text, run in the cairn repo root). It edits only cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py: _carry returns a copy of _check's result and, when healthy is False, adds a 'finding' string — 'the trouble panel's route failed: <error>' when _check recorded an error, else 'the cairn device declares no trouble pane' when no pane is declared, else 'the trouble pane's handler did not come back with a list'. A healthy carry has no 'finding' key. _check is unchanged. No other code changes.

D3: SETTLED: the proof cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_trouble_panel.py is already on disk and committed (6b4b2dbc, f43d20a0) with PROVES for this ticket: clause 1 test_websocket_route_exists, clause 2 test_an_UNHEALTHY_probe_NAMES_ITS_FINDING (red before the patch, green after), clause 3 test_the_panel_is_the_CAIRN_devices_not_the_hosts. After the patch `python3 -m pytest cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_trouble_panel.py` shows 16 passed. Regression: `python3 cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_cairn_probes_report_to_the_watch.py` is run and its result recorded, whatever it is (it reds while this ticket stands at FIXME; that red is not this build's to change).

D4: SETTLED: clauses 4 (detail not truncated) and 5 (the panel says it is read-only) are measured RED in the world (cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:271 static detail hint, :417 ellipsis, no read-only text) and their code is the web_server device's, so under RULE 1 they are built by a child code-seam on cairn/devices/web_server, not in this build. This ticket crosses BUILDME and PROVEME, then waits for that child to be PROVED before its own PROVED.

FIXME 1 answered: the WATCHME finding 'the probe reads its ticket's falsifier as failing and its carry names no finding' is repaired by D2 — the probe's carry names its failing condition as 'finding' (route error, no pane declared, or no list), proved by test_an_UNHEALTHY_probe_NAMES_ITS_FINDING. The failing pulse itself came from a scratch bus (cairn-bus-bedf9ef0c9, commons journal 2026-10-05T10:38:32Z), not the live one, which reads healthy (63 live troubles, 2026-10-06); a test-marked message moving a live record is step 5's to close.
SETTLED: after the proof shows 16 passed, commit the patched probe module with the history, state and journal the BUILDME crossing wrote, in one cairn commit naming 7a1265439f54

SETTLED: this build takes NO action on the scratch-bus write; the journal line stays as recorded (records are append-only). Closing that path is step 5's proof, a different ticket; the builder of 7a1265439f54 only applies D2 and runs D3

D4 child, SETTLED: the child code-seam on cairn/devices/web_server is 1cafb10c2983 (the-trouble-pane-shows-the-whole-finding), PROVED 2026-10-06 with proof cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_the_trouble_pane_shows_the_whole_finding.py. This build does NOT touch web_server. Clauses (4) and (5) are not this build's to make green; after PROVEME the PROVES for (4)/(5) naming the child's teeth is the ticket's proof bookkeeping, done by the PROVED step, not the builder.

D6 files, SETTLED: from the cairn repo root, git add cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py cairn/devices/cairn/history.json cairn/devices/cairn/state.json .artifact-journal.jsonl && git commit -m '7a1265439f54: BUILDME — the trouble-panel probe names its finding'. The pre-commit hook runs the artifact check itself.

D3 recording, SETTLED: nothing records the regression's result automatically. 'Recorded' means: write the regression's pass/fail count and exit code as one line in the body of the D6 commit message (e.g. 'test_cairn_probes_report_to_the_watch: exit 1, 1 failed / 3 passed'). No file is written for it.
